requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its own anchored definition on the current page. The badge MUST have a separate adjacent link containing an accessible right-arrow icon in an integrated segment matching the badge color linking to its evidence detail page. The badge and arrow MUST remain aligned in one non-wrapping row. Definitions MUST NOT be followed by a separate plaintext evidence link. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
Every MUST in `requirements.index.navigation` has implementing code and a test that checks it. I found no gaps and no `{fixme}` references.

- **Definition badge links to its own anchor:** `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` emits `id="habeas-{kind}-{name}"` and `href="#…"`. `src/lib.rs#impl[DefinitionKind]/fn[anchor]` builds the same anchor for links from other pages. `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` asserts the pair for `req`, `example` and `cli.mdbook`.
- **Separate adjacent arrow link in the badge color:** `replace_definitions` emits `a.habeas-detail-icon` with `background-color` set to the badge color, an `aria-label`, and an SVG arrow marked `aria-hidden`. It links to the detail page through `chapter_href`. `definition_badge_and_evidence_icon_share_colors` checks the color match. `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` and `definition_evidence_link_targets_are_escaped` check the `aria-label` and `href`.
- **One non-wrapping row:** `md/habeas.css` sets `inline-flex`, `flex-wrap: nowrap` and `white-space: nowrap` on `.habeas-definition-badge`. It also sets `flex-shrink: 0` on the links and gives the icon its size and centering. `definition_badge_stylesheet_keeps_the_arrow_in_one_row` reads the shipped CSS and asserts these declarations.
- **No plaintext evidence link:** `replace_definitions` emits only the badge and icon in the wrapper span. Two tests assert the output lacks "See evidence".
- **Detail page links to the anchored definition and to the index:** `src/index.rs#fn[render_detail_page]` emits `[Requirements index](…) · [View definition](…#anchor)`. `src/index.rs#impl[DetailPlan]/fn[populate]` always passes the index path. `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` and the `lib.rs` tests assert both links, including for nested chapters.
- **Reference badges still link to the definition:** `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_badge]`, called from `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_inline_references]`, builds the link with `chapter_href`. `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` asserts the `href` for impl, cite and test badges.
- **Names containing `.md`:** `src/lib.rs#fn[chapter_href]` rewrites `.md` to `%2Emd`, and `replace_definitions` does the same for the permalink. `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` tests `chapter_href` directly. The `cli.mdbook` cases in the other tests check the badge, detail and definition links.

Everything reached from the `{impl}` items is covered: `chapter_href`, `anchor`, `render_detail_page` and the `populate` wiring. I found no unspecified extra behavior. `render_detail_page` accepts `index_path: None`, but only tests call it that way. The production caller always passes the index.
